met_analysis:
The low pressure area over northwest Madhya Pradesh & adjoining southwest Uttar Pradesh persisted over the same region at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 05th September 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height. It is likely to move east- northeastwards during next 2 days.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Anupgarh, Alwar, centre of low pressure area over northwest Madhya Pradesh & adjoining southwest Uttar Pradesh, Sidhi, Daltonganj, Bankura and thence eastwards towards Tripura.
The trough from South Haryana to south Assam across the cyclonic circulation associated with low pressure area over northwest Madhya Pradesh & adjoining southwest Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, northern part of Gangetic West Bengal and Bangladesh at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from south Gujarat to north Bangladesh across cyclonic circulation associated with low pressure area over northwest Madhya Pradesh & adjoining southwest Uttar Pradesh, north Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and West Bengal between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle and upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 28°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from south Telangana to Gulf of Mannar across Rayalaseema and Tamil Nadu at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over north Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam & Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over coastal Tamil Nadu & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengalat 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
